name: landlord-db-fresh
note: rewritten in full every refresh run (whole dict re-saved), so mtime is a true run signal. >50h = the DB stopped updating (froze for 5 days once).

name: tenant-db-fresh
note: full re-save every run, same as landlord-db

name: discovery-candidates-fresh
note: written unconditionally by discovery_candidates.py each refresh slot; the sustained zero-scan case is owned by discovery_watchdog

name: matchmaker-data-fresh
note: rebuilt by the matchmaker refresh slots; rental-db-watchdog checks the DEPLOYED app, this checks the local data file

name: fsbo-state-fresh
note: FSBO scraper writes its state each nightly 00:00 run; feeds the do-not-engage guardrail. Stale = scraper stopped and the guardrail is going stale unwatched.

name: landlord-sheet-synced-fresh
note: Google Sheet push marker, stamped each successful sync (a true run marker). This push was silently stale for weeks in July; a freshness check makes a future stall visible same-day.

name: wa-touchpoint-sync-fresh
note: touched-state marker updated each touchpoint-sync run; known-fragile area, so worth output-freshness visibility.

name: public-listings-fresh
note: listings-nightly (00:30) syncs this from the landlord DB. UNCERTAIN whether it rewrites unconditionally or only on change, so window is generous (72h) to avoid a quiet-period false alarm; it still catches a multi-day stall. Currently ~50h old (synced_at 2 Sep) — worth confirming listings-nightly is running. A run-marker for listings-nightly would let this window tighten (see output-contract note).
